requirements.statement: Ledger balance validation must compare exact per-currency sums, not modular Int64 sums; in the database a commerce ledger transaction is created as draft, posts only with entries that sum to zero in every currency, keeps its entries unchanged once posted, never returns to draft, and is reversed only by a posted transaction.
requirements.authority: approved AUTHORITY-069
requirements.property: per-currency accumulated sum uses arbitrary precision
requirements.verification: Integer type and inspected conversion before accumulation; 512 actual-module boundary sequences and Hspec regressions for the helper. Runtime SQL posting check exercised on the production schema (balanced, unbalanced, cross-currency, [M,M,2] wrap, extreme balanced, empty) with a disabled-trigger negative control. Bounded TLC model of ledger posting with five negative controls and the ledger-posting-postgresql spec against the fully migrated schema (formal/system/ledger-posting.md). Legacy-upgrade fixtures and witnessed two-session reversal races under READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ run in scripts/__tests__/ledger-posting-upgrade.py. The canonical provider retry/refund harness applies both the ledger integrity and fixed-line snapshot migrations before its store integration cases; its reduced domain fixture does not establish every production-domain guard (docs/payments/consolidation-2026-10-15.md). Snapshot schedules in ledger-posting-snapshot.py test entry INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE before posting (blocked and already committed), post-first and writer rollback, across READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE. Six lock-only mutation controls reproduce posted balance 1; these finite PostgreSQL tests do not discharge complete implementation/refinement obligations. Non-owner TEMP and caller-schema shadowing checks plus two lookup-removal controls exercise the installed guards; the finite LedgerNamespace model abstracts these lookup choices (formal/system/ledger-namespace.md). The startup schema verifier rejects missing, reordered or caller-controlled lookup settings, missing expected function signatures and SECURITY DEFINER drift for both installed ledger guards. Transaction-scoped full-schema mutations and a compatible extra-GUC case run through the actual rendered verifier; migration receipts remain unchanged. Changes to the installed schema verifier, ledger/provider/expiry runners and ledger regression harnesses must select backend=true, so the full-schema PostgreSQL controls are executed rather than silently skipped. The path-classifier regression checks nine affected paths against the real selector.

Database: SQLSTATE 23514 for creation in any status but draft, posting without entries or unbalanced in any currency, entries inserted/updated/deleted after posting, posted -> draft, draft -> reversed, reversal by a non-posted transaction, and any change of a reversed transaction. A referenced posted reverser cannot itself be reversed. Migration rejects existing empty/unbalanced posted rows and self, draft or reversed reversal targets before installing new guards. Stale snapshot posting or entry mutation may return SQLSTATE 40001; callers must roll back the whole transaction. The additive write-fence migration separately refuses empty or unbalanced posted/reversed history.
requirements.recovery: Preserve existing evidence. Migration fails before replacing guards if posted history is empty or unbalanced or a reversed transaction lacks a distinct posted reverser. validateLedgerBalance (Haskell) has no runtime caller; the database rule is the enforced one.

Before 2026-10-12 the database validated balance only on draft -> posted, so a transaction inserted as posted or an entry appended after posting was not rejected; the ledger posting integrity migration closes both.

The #551 lock-only entry guard admitted stale-snapshot unbalanced postings under REPEATABLE READ. The additive 2026-10-16 write fence repairs the reproduced schedules; unbounded SQL/MVCC refinement, caller retry policy and deployed correspondence remain open.

Unqualified trigger lookup admitted non-owner TEMP shadowing on source 59df1dd2a17952b906cf89d1c5502725d51239e1. The additive namespace migration pins both functions; runtime trusted-schema privileges, owner/DDL bypass and deployed correspondence remain unverified.

Startup verification checks the installed trusted lookup settings and invoker boundary, not arbitrary trigger bodies or privileged DDL equivalence; a table owner can still disable or replace triggers.

requirements.title: Consolidate authoritative ticket admission, inventory and transfer boundaries
requirements.statement: Ticket admission must consume a paid issued unused event-scoped ticket at most once with its audit in the same transaction; inventory holds must respect tier/event capacity; accepted transfer must rotate the credential and revoke former-holder projection. Checkout quantity must not exceed the approved versioned per-order limit; approved/retired commercial policies cannot regress to draft or lose immutable history. Approved tax-inclusive pricing must preserve advertised integer totals for every accepted quantity, conserve total = organizer payable + platform fees + tax, and retain the purchased mode immutably; an event-specific tax rate is independently authorized. An unresolved signed-provider refund or reversal bound to the same checkout/capture/merchant must fence admission even when legacy rows still say paid and issued. PayPal capture requires an authenticated readback of the original provider order, with unchanged internal-order, merchant, amount and currency validation before marking paid. Zero platform fees must create no zero-valued ledger entry while cash, organizer payable, tax and nonzero fees conserve the captured total. A verified external refund/reversal received before capture binding leaves durable merchant-scoped evidence after inbox retry exhaustion; later binding must fence admission without a webhook replay. Canonical orders reject legacy bulk status mutations. Refund routing follows the unique succeeded provider, retaining existing non-PayPal request behavior. Retained issued tickets of partially refunded orders remain transferable under the purchased policy. OAuth failure before a refund POST leaves the request retryable; ambiguous POST outcomes retain the no-repeat fence. Accepted provider refund identities survive mismatched monetary responses so exact authenticated readback can reconcile without another POST. Whole-ticket partial refunds accept any eligible subset matching the stable cent allocation. An authorized guest order receipt remains accessible when public ticket sales close; receipt lookup failure must not offer a replacement purchase. Ticket Stripe initialization failures return a bounded generic service-unavailable response instead of exposing upstream diagnostic bodies to buyers; existing automatic method selection is preserved. Legacy Stripe refund approval must commit a single pending-to-processing claim before provider execution; ambiguous responses never reopen the request, and rejection must condition its write on current pending state. Legacy Stripe completion additionally requires a succeeded refund object with exact requested amount, currency and PaymentIntent; observed provider IDs are retained while unverified evidence remains processing without ticket or inventory completion effects. Legacy Stripe inventory completion requires a positive order quantity and one atomic event/tier-bound decrement guarded by sufficient current sold stock; an unsuccessful release rolls back completion while retaining processing and observed evidence. Legacy refund request creation must serialize the absence check and insertion with current event/order authority and paid amount, preserving one-request rejection on the legacy route and canonical successive allocations. New direct, legacy Stripe and public canonical ticket reservations must validate current sale and promotion windows against the same fresh database wall-time sample after their final admission locks, retaining inclusive endpoints, stored orders and existing reuse behavior.

Attempt retry: Haskell probe tests (stale-then-live, budget exhaustion, final negative result, cancellation through retry) (the mutations include single attempt, no retry and cancellation swallowed in the retry; the attempt budget is bound to the pool size plus one); the PostgreSQL harness first leaves more idle pooled connections than it makes degraded probes, so the probes must discard the terminated connections within their own attempts (with one attempt per probe the recovery probe took the next terminated connection and failed, 2026-10-12). requirements.title: Rejected interaction writes consume the exact per-account minute budget
requirements.statement: Authenticated interaction write attempts consume a durable per-account calendar-minute counter after the session is confirmed and before the write runs. requirements.title: Observe the public ticket funnel without exporting private ticket data
requirements.statement: The existing web analytics client observes the ticket funnel using public identifiers and bounded metadata; payment completion and ticket display observations require the corresponding server checkout states. Browser telemetry never becomes financial or admission authority. Every backend-created hosted payment session counts as initiation, including prepared, failed and confirmed-no-charge outcomes; initiation deduplicates per order/provider. Direct event and checkout landing UTMs replace stale campaign attribution before observation, without persisting private order paths or lookup parameters; disabled analytics stores no attribution. When the TDF storefront is closed for an event (no approved price policy, no tiers, sold out), public surfaces never render an empty order form: they localise the server reason and, for imported events, link to the external ticket vendor recovered from the published description.

requirements.title: Issue an SRI electronic invoice for every paid invoiced ticket order
requirements.statement: A ticket policy may require electronic invoices. Such an event cannot sell until invoicing is configured for its checkout environment and the submission worker is switched on. Each paid order enqueues exactly one invoice with the next sequential number; the worker binds a TDF-generated access key and submits through an authorized provider, never resending a submission whose outcome is unknown. Every verified refund of an invoiced order enqueues exactly one credit note bound to the invoice; bank-transfer orders are refunded by staff with separation of duties.

requirements.privacy: Identification only when required by the SRI USD 50 rule; credentials stay in server configuration and are redacted from stored errors.
requirements.concurrency: Issuer point row lock for numbering; SKIP LOCKED claims; a submission starts only through one statement bound to the claimer's lease and an unset submission mark; every result is written under the claimer's lease token.
requirements.idempotency: Unique invoice per order; stable access key per document; paid re-transitions do not enqueue again.
requirements.failure: Validation refusal -> failed, whatever the length of the provider's message; unknown transport outcome of a submission -> uncertain; a status query that fails, is refused or is unreadable, or an internal error while polling, leaves the document submitted for a later query.
requirements.recovery: Administrators resend failed documents after fixing configuration; uncertain documents are reconciled in the provider.
requirements.observability: Staff invoice list with status, number, access key, authorization and last error.
requirements.property: Every paid order of an invoiced policy has exactly one invoice document whose identity never changes.

requirements.statement: A public consent request must not activate WhatsApp consent. It records a pending request; claiming a confirmation request is one conditional update allowed only when the number has no request in the last 24 hours, and simultaneous first requests for a number do not fail. A request the provider did not accept stays pending as undelivered: for 1 hour from the request the number can still confirm it by messaging first and a new public request may retry the send without changing the request instant; afterwards it waits for the 24-hour interval. Delivered requests to a number are therefore at least 23 hours apart. Consent becomes active only through one conditional update when the same number sends an affirmative keyword whose Meta message timestamp is no earlier than the pending request, within 7 days of a delivered request, and the request has not been withdrawn since; a concurrent withdrawal wins and a delayed or replayed earlier reply cannot confirm a newer request. The confirmation request uses the approved template named by WHATSAPP_CONSENT_TEMPLATE when configured; the person may also message SI first (VITE_WHATSAPP_OPTIN_URL). Public responses never disclose a number's consent state; the public consent lookup returns 410 without reading consent data. Opt-out (public form, inbound STOP/SALIR/BAJA/CANCELAR or staff revocation) always withdraws consent and invalidates any pending request without resetting the 24-hour interval, and its stored instant is never earlier than the request it defeats; neither withdrawing, confirming nor staff capture lets anyone request another message early. The public opt-out notifies only a number that was subscribed. The failure of a superseded send attempt changes nothing. Staff consent capture remains admin-only.

requirements.authorization: Only the number's own reply (verified Meta webhook signature) or an Admin can activate consent.
requirements.privacy: Public responses are identical regardless of prior state; display names are not returned publicly.

requirements.idempotency: Repeated replies after activation are no-ops; repeated requests within 24 hours of a request send nothing unless they retry an undelivered request inside its hour; a send failure is bound to its own request instant.
requirements.failure: A WhatsApp send failure is recorded on the outgoing message and marks only its own request undelivered; consent is unaffected. The signed confirmation fixture requires HTTP200, consent activation and one recorded notice. The historical phone/timestamp collision is removed by the existing index-declaration migration; a separate notice clock sample alone was only best-effort on the old schema.
requirements.recovery: A number can request again 24 hours after its last request instant, or retry an undelivered, unwithdrawn request within 1 hour.

The 1-hour window for an undelivered request is an engineering default chosen because the number never saw a prompt; the product owner has not confirmed the duration.
A provider failure that hides an actual delivery (ambiguous timeout) is treated as undelivered and could allow a second request inside the interval.

A withdrawn request cannot be replaced until 24 hours after its request instant. An undelivered request that is neither confirmed nor retried within 1 hour waits for the 24-hour interval even though nothing was delivered.

Provider notice delivery and durable retry after an accepted inbound receipt are separate obligations; the existing index-declaration migration supersedes the historical same-timestamp uniqueness hazards without establishing exactly-once provider delivery.

requirements.title: Canonical music releases with immutable approved versions
requirements.statement: Music releases are authored as versions owned by a verified artist or authorized team. Each version moves only through music_valid_transition; approval freezes an immutable snapshot and SHA-256; correcting a published release creates a related version that references the same immutable asset bytes. Publication and withdrawal are applied by locked database functions that handle each due candidate on its own: a candidate that fails at publication is suspended with its error and the other candidates still publish; publishing a version retires every other formerly published version of its release that is still published, replacement_pending or takedown_scheduled, and reopens a withdrawn release; a failure that is transient (deadlock, serialization failure, lock timeout) leaves the candidate scheduled for the next run; the release points at the version it last published only while that version is published, suspended, replacement_pending or takedown_scheduled. Only a published, in-embargo-window, territory-allowed version is public.

requirements.title: Quarantined uploads, reproducible processing and signed asset access
requirements.statement: Audio and artwork uploads go by scoped SigV4 multipart to a quarantine bucket under a UUID key. The worker re-downloads, recomputes SHA-256, inspects the real type, produces reproducible derivatives (AAC/FLAC/preview/artwork) with a versioned manifest, and only then promotes the original bytes as immutable. Public asset URLs are signed for five minutes only after music_public_asset_accessible re-resolves version, embargo, territory and policy; masters are never publicly signed.

Orphan multipart uploads created by the worker's own PUTs are aborted per worker-multipart.md; client upload sessions have no purge (ambiguity). After a checksum-mismatch dead letter, uploading the correct bytes under the same declared hash is inspected and the earlier attempts, running ones included, are cancelled (2026-10-12_music_upload_rebind).

requirements.title: Private reproducible DDEX ERN 4.3.2 export of approved versions
requirements.statement: A DDEX ERN 4.3.2 message is a projection of one approved version snapshot hash. The API commits export and job atomically, serializes per actor/key and version, revalidates queued exports against the same rules used by API, renderer and worker, and produces a private, reproducible package with message-bound file names. No delivery to partners is performed.

Worker gate 2 (rules re-checked, same snapshot hash): generating -> valid with xml/manifest/package assets, then job succeeded
Any failure of an attempt: not-valid export -> validation_failed and job retry; on the last attempt -> failed and job dead_letter, in one write
A valid export whose job did not close is recovered as is: job succeeded, nothing regenerated
Authorized replay of the original request: a queued export without a job gets its job; otherwise the existing export is returned unchanged

Export job committed without its export row
valid -> any other status; a valid package is never regenerated or re-pointed

requirements.privacy: Packages are private and contain collaborator identifiers; never public.
requirements.concurrency: API: pg_advisory_xact_lock(music-ddex:<actor>:<key>) then the version row FOR UPDATE; export and job commit together. Worker: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim; every later statement runs under pg_temp.music_worker_guard (version FOR NO KEY UPDATE, job FOR UPDATE, status running, same worker name, claimed attempt as fencing token, lease younger than the ttl); a running job is reclaimed only after its lease expired. Gate 1 and gate 2 lock both registry rows FOR SHARE in UUID order and share their transaction with the status write. Bounded model: MusicDdexExport.tla.
requirements.idempotency: Replaying the request with the same actor, key, version, operation, sender and recipient returns the existing export; a different body under the same key is 409; the natural key (version, recipient, operation, snapshot) is unique, so a second request for the same package is 409 whatever its key. The replay recreates only a missing job of a queued export and never resets attempts.
requirements.failure: A gate refusal stores the field-level report (valid=false, code ddex_preconditions_failed, errors[]). Any other failure of an attempt (renderer, transfer, checksum, crash handler) stores a fixed message with its error code; the worker's stderr summary is kept on the job row until the next claim clears it, and permanently once dead-lettered. The export becomes validation_failed while attempts remain and failed with the dead letter; a valid or failed export is never changed by a later attempt.
requirements.recovery: Queued revalidation and replay per ddex-queued-validation.md and ddex-atomic-enqueue.md; a valid export is recovered without regeneration after a crash between gate 2 and job closure. A failed (dead-lettered) export has no recovery path: see ambiguity.
requirements.observability: Export status and validation report (release downloaders); job status, attempts, error code and stderr summary (operators).
requirements.verification: ERN spec against fixture and schema, package builder tests, enqueue fault-injection probe. Bounded TLA+ model of the export/job lifecycle under two leased processes with five single-guard negative controls (formal/system/music-ddex-export.md). Worker runtime test (PostgreSQL, substitute renderer/packager/transport): commit gate, revocation during rendering, valid recovery, queued revalidation, and the processing-failure report that excludes worker stderr and recovers to valid on retry.

ambiguity: Partner-specific profiles and delivery are out of scope; compatibility matrix is a 2026-09-12 snapshot.

A dead-lettered export (status failed) has no recovery path: the natural unique key (version, recipient, operation, snapshot) rejects a new request for the same package and the replay never re-enqueues a failed export, so a transient outage lasting the five attempts (about 15 minutes) blocks that operation for that version and recipient until an operator edits the rows. The same holds for any non-queued export whose job was cancelled by hand. ADR-018 chose no blind retry; an audited operator retry is an open product decision.
The job's stderr summary is served to the uploader through the upload status endpoint (MusicReleaseUpload.hs); that surface belongs to MEDIA-MUSIC-ASSET-001 and is not changed here.
The export's validation_failed status is also used for processing failures that are not validation refusals; the report's code distinguishes them.

conformance.reason: Lifecycle, fencing, finality and failure-report privacy are modelled within bounds and exercised by the worker runtime test locally; the export feature flag is off in production, and dead-letter recovery is undecided.

requirements.title: Music downloads only through verified purchase entitlements
requirements.statement: A music purchase order references one rule, release version and price in integer minor units and opens a commerce checkout session in the music_download domain. Only server-verified provider evidence bound to the order marks it paid; the projection settles a payable purchase and grants exactly one entitlement, ending it on refund or chargeback. Verified money for a closed purchase follows PAY-MUSIC-OUTCOME-001 and grants no entitlement. Entitled and free downloads use the same downloadable-asset predicate, count each new request identifier against the entitlement limit, answer a repeated identifier only while its signed URL is valid, and issue URLs that live 300 seconds. A free grant that was revoked is not revived by a new request. Purchase creation admits the rule only when its asset belongs to the offered release version and satisfies the same downloadable-asset predicate at the offer query snapshot; rejection creates no purchase.
requirements.authority: Unreviewed recovered local implementation; ADR-005 in docs/music-releases/architecture-and-data-model.md
requirements.source: Local main work of 2026-09-11..2026-09-16 recovered onto main in PR #510; docs/music-releases/architecture-and-data-model.md
requirements.property: A purchase entitlement is granted once, by the paid transition of a checkout carrying bound verified evidence, and a download URL is issued only for an active entitlement of the requesting buyer within its counted limit. At purchase offer admission, asset.release_version_id equals the offered release version and the existing shared downloadable-asset predicate is true.

requirements.title: Negotiable offers with slot accounting on seeking and offering classifieds
requirements.statement: Every classified category declares an intent (seeking or offering) that search exposes and filters by. A classified declares slots (1-100), a price mode (open, suggested, fixed), an optional offer deadline and structured terms. An application is an offer carrying an amount, currency, terms and expiry; counter-offers alternate strictly between the classified author and the offerer through recorded rounds (at most ten; fixed prices admit none), only the participant who did not make the last move may accept, acceptance consumes exactly one slot atomically and freezes the accepted amount, exhausting the slots fills the classified and rejects every open offer with reason slots_filled, closing a classified rejects open offers with reason classified_closed, withdrawing an accepted offer releases its slot, and the public sees only an anonymous offer count and range.

any open state -> rejected (author or closure), withdrawn (offerer) or expired (system)
accepted|conversation_open -> withdrawn (releases the slot)

Acceptance records accepted_amount_minor and decrements slots_remaining in the same transaction
Filling or closing a classified rejects open offers with a reason and notifies offerers
Public classified projections expose intent, price mode, slots, deadline, terms and anonymous offer statistics

requirements.privacy: Offer amounts and messages stay private to participants; the public range appears only with at least three offers and never identifies offerers; terms carry a textual place, never an exact private address.
requirements.concurrency: Slot consumption is a guarded UPDATE (slots_remaining > 0) inside the acceptance transaction; the round number is unique per offer; idempotency keys cover offers and counters.
requirements.idempotency: Offer and counter requests require Idempotency-Key with request fingerprints; replays return the existing offer; backfill of initial rounds is idempotent.
requirements.failure: Turn, slot, deadline, fixed-price and duplicate violations return 409; malformed amounts, terms or expiry return 400; counters without the runtime flag return 503; an expired offer is marked expired and the transition rejected.
requirements.recovery: Rollback 2026-11-08_marketplace_offers_rollback maps counter states to viewed/submitted, expired to withdrawn, keeps the latest amount as proposed_amount_minor and restores the previous notification allowlist.
requirements.observability: directory_audit_event rows for rounds, acceptances and bulk rejections; analytics events application_submitted, offer_countered, offer_accepted, match_converted; in-app notifications marketplace.offer.* and marketplace.classified.filled; release schema verification of the new objects.

requirements.title: Marketplace agreements with frozen commission and deposit, created from accepted offers
requirements.statement: With the marketplace.agreements gate on, accepting an offer that carries a positive amount and a currency creates exactly one agreement in the acceptance transaction. The buyer is the party that seeks (the classified author for seeking categories, the offerer for offering categories) and the other party is the provider. The agreement freezes the amount, currency, combined terms, the TDF commission and the deposit/balance split from the pricing rule in force (default 10% commission, 30% deposit), and those values never change. Part A collects no payment: agreements start confirmed and off-platform. The provider marks the start, only the buyer confirms completion, either party cancels or disputes a live agreement and only an administrator resolves a dispute. Completion records a verified interaction that makes both parties eligible to review each other; cancellation withdraws the accepted offer and releases its slot; withdrawing an accepted offer cancels its live agreement.

requirements.title: Marketplace agreement payments on the canonical checkout with a frozen split per charge
requirements.statement: With the marketplace.agreement_payments gate on, an agreement whose provider profile has a ready payout account usable in the agreed currency and whose deposit is positive starts pending_deposit and settled on the platform, with a deposit deadline from the pricing rule; otherwise it starts confirmed and off-platform as in MKT-AGREEMENT-001. The buyer starts the charge the agreement is waiting for (the deposit while pending_deposit, the balance while balance_due). Each charge is one marketplace_agreement_payment row bound to one canonical checkout of domain marketplace_agreement, and freezes its split: the TDF commission due on that charge (as much of the frozen commission as fits in the deposit; on the balance, whatever the paid charges did not actually collect for the platform), the estimated processor fee borne by the configured payer (the service provider by default), and the provider amount, adding up exactly to the charge. Only verified provider evidence bound to that checkout marks a charge paid; a paid deposit confirms the agreement and a paid balance completes it and records the verified interaction. The buyer's confirmation of delivery waits for the balance when one is owed. A participant cannot cancel directly, nor by withdrawing the accepted offer, once a deposit was collected or while a payment attempt may still collect money. A deposit unpaid at its deadline expires the agreement and releases the slot, when a participant loads agreements and every five minutes from a background job. Disputed agreements are listed for administrators, oldest dispute first, with who opened the dispute, from which state and why. TDF never holds the provider's part: the agreement domain routes as a marketplace product flow, which requires verified connected-account, split and payout capabilities, and the shared executor refuses agreement checkouts until a split-capable provider flow exists.

requirements.title: Public-course-only index refresh
requirements.statement: RAG index checks and refreshes shall first remove legacy non-course derived chunks independently of freshness, embedding configuration or provider availability. Refreshes shall embed only public course fields, atomically replace the public index on success (including an empty corpus without a provider call), and preserve the previous public index on provider or persistence failure.
preconditions: The configured embedding model and database vector dimensions agree.
Course fields exposed by the public course contract are approved public material.
inputs: Up to 50 route-eligible canonical course rows ordered by updated_at descending

state.initial: The historical index may include private sources.

allowedTransitions: Commit non-course derived-index cleanup before checking freshness or validating embedding configuration.
Collect public course fields, chunk and embed them.
Replace all derived index rows after a complete successful embedding response.
Clear the index without embedding when the captured corpus is empty.
Reject a failed refresh while retaining the previous public index; committed legacy cleanup is not undone.
forbiddenTransitions: Include bookings, availability, campaigns, ads, services, resources, rooms or studio notes in refresh embedding payloads.
Report an empty refresh as successful while retaining old chunks.
Commit public-index deletion if replacement insertion fails.
Skip legacy cleanup because the index is fresh or an embedding provider/configuration is unavailable.
Raw rejected stored URLs or route-unreachable course identities -> embedding payload.
Disclose a captured production identity shared by multiple Text-normalized stored course rows.
effects: The next admitted worker check or administrator refresh removes legacy non-course chunks locally without a provider call; public replacement remains a separate transaction.
Source entities are not deleted; external provider records and backups are not erased by reindexing.
requirements.authorization: Existing administrator and worker admission remains unchanged. Index source selection is enforced in the backend, independently of retrieval guards.
requirements.privacy: Explicit product decision on 2026-10-13: public courses only; stop indexing private material. This policy concerns index refreshes, not a claim that query embeddings or other assistant provider payloads are public.
requirements.concurrency: One refresh captures public documents from statement snapshots before embedding and atomically replaces the index. Parallel refresh ordering/freshness is not guaranteed; all revised writers still construct only course chunks. Retrieval separately checks current course metadata. Cleanup and replacement are separate transactions. Deployment must drain old mixed-source writers; no claim covers privileged external SQL writers or rollback to the old builder. Each constructed document reads its fields, earliest session and collision inputs in one SELECT snapshot.
requirements.idempotency: Repeated successful refreshes replace the derived index; provider requests may repeat and chunk identifiers/timestamps are not stable.
requirements.failure: Cleanup SQL failure aborts before embedding. Model/schema mismatch and provider/count errors return Left after legacy cleanup; replacement SQL errors propagate after rollback of public replacement. A missing index table skips cleanup and fails existing schema validation.
requirements.recovery: Retry failed public refreshes while retaining existing public chunks. Do not restore non-course chunks or roll back to a mixed-source builder. Historical backups and provider-held data require separate retention/erasure decisions.
requirements.observability: PostgreSQL tests capture adapter payloads and persisted rows, check empty-corpus no-call behavior, provider/count refusal and SQL rollback. Existing administrator result and index statistics report refresh outcome. Aggregate source counts verify cleanup without disclosing content; tests cover a fresh index and invalid configuration before provider admission.
requirements.source: Explicit user product decision 2026-10-13: Public courses only; stop indexing private material (Recommended).
requirements.confidence: medium
ambiguity: Historical external provider retention/erasure requires separate evidence.
Concurrent refresh ordering and index freshness are not serialized by this change.

conformance.reason: Implementation, bounded model and PostgreSQL regression checks are mapped; exact candidate and deployed verification remain required. Historical provider retention is outside the refresh boundary.

requirements.title: Public artist tips: addressed artist, listing admission and recorded outcome
requirements.statement: POST /fans/artists/{artistId}/tips addresses the artist by PartyId, as every sibling /fans/artists route and the public apArtistId do. A tip is admitted only for an artist the public directory currently lists (its directory identity is published, public, allowed and not merged, or it has no directory identity) and whose payout account is complete; funds are routed only to that artist's own connected account with a 10% platform fee rounded down. An unavailable provider stores nothing. Provider error text is never returned to the caller. An optional Idempotency-Key (1..128 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores) binds the request fingerprint: the same key with the same request replays the stored tip and its PaymentIntent (client secret retrieved from Stripe, never stored), the same key with a different request, a failed attempt or an attempt without a PaymentIntent is a 409, and concurrent duplicates are serialized by a unique index per artist and key. A recorded tip outcome changes only from pending, by a conditional update, so duplicated, reordered or concurrent webhook deliveries never replace it.

requirements.title: Provider event lease writes are fenced by the claimed attempt
requirements.statement: A provider event in commerce_provider_event_inbox is claimed with a lease that increments attempt_count; a lease older than fifteen minutes may be reclaimed. Every outcome write (processed, ignored, retry, dead_letter) requires processing_status = 'processing' AND attempt_count equal to the writer's claimed attempt, so a worker whose lease was reclaimed can no longer record an outcome over the current holder's lease. A terminal status is always the one written by the latest lease holder, and a successful outcome of the latest lease holder is never lost.

preconditions: commerce_provider_event_inbox with processing_started_at and attempt_count (2026-08-14 migrations).
allowedTransitions: pending|retry|stale processing -> processing (attempt_count + 1)
processing -> processed|ignored|retry|dead_letter by the holder of the current attempt only
retry -> dead_letter when attempt_count reaches 8
forbiddenTransitions: an outcome written by a worker whose attempt is not the current attempt_count
processed|ignored|dead_letter -> any other status by a worker
effects: Conditional UPDATE fenced by attempt_count on every lease write.
requirements.authorization: Workers and the inline handler only; events need verified signatures in production (schema CHECK).
requirements.privacy: Error summaries are sanitized to printable text, 500 characters.
requirements.concurrency: Stale reclaim after fifteen minutes is intentional; the fence makes the reclaimed worker's late write a no-op. The side effect it already performed (payment admission) is idempotent under PAY-RETRY-001 and PAY-CAPTURE-RECON-001.
requirements.idempotency: Event id unique per provider, environment and merchant; outcome writes idempotent under the fence.
requirements.failure: Decryption or processing exceptions mark retry with exponential backoff up to 3600 seconds; the eighth attempt dead-letters.
requirements.recovery: Dead letters are replayed by operations (operations-failure-replay.md).
requirements.observability: attempt_count, last_attempt_at, processing_started_at, error_summary.
requirements.verification: Bounded TLC with three workers and a negative control reproducing the stale-reclaim overwrite; Apalache inductive proof for any nonempty set of up to three workers, attempt budgets 1..8 and claim bounds 1..8; PostgreSQL-backed ProviderRetrySpec exercises claim, retry exhaustion and processed replay.
requirements.evidence: scripts/verify-inductive-proofs.sh output; tdf-hq-test ProviderRetrySpec run with a database.

requirements.statement: Cancelling a Domo quote after money was collected refunds according to the single approved domo_cancellation_policy version: cancellation by TDF refunds everything collected; customer cancellation refunds the collected balance in full and the deposit by lead time (whole 24-hour periods before the event start; at or above full_refund_min_days: all; at or above partial_refund_min_days: deposit minus partial_retained_bps rounded half up; below, or once the event is in progress: nothing). When a succeeded PaymentIntent with a positive amount matches a ticket order but fails the binding or evidence validation, the handler still answers 400 and first commits an open commerce_reconciliation_exception (provider stripe, verified_payment_not_admitted, internal reference event_ticket_order:{id}, expected and received amounts). Z3 proof stripe_ticket_capture.py (translation of handleStripePaymentIntentSucceeded for a matched ticket order, validateStripeTicketPaymentEvidence, parseStripeTicketCapture and stripeTicketClosedOrderNeedsReview, pinned by the hash of those regions): tickets are issued only with the full binding on a pending order, the answer is 400 exactly when the binding is not admitted, a succeeded positive capture always ends in tickets, a paid redelivery or an open exception, and each comparison, the pending fence, both exception writes and the review of a missing order row are load-bearing. requirements.title: A session invoice and its SRI document are issued at most once per request
requirements.statement: POST /invoices/{sessionId}/generate must not issue a second SRI electronic invoice for a retried, doubled or concurrent request. Issuing to SRI requires an idempotencyKey; the same key and request returns the stored answer, a different request with the key is refused, and an unanswered reservation refuses replays instead of issuing again. The SRI script output is accepted only when it validates against the request.
requirements.authority: Formal audit 2026-10-31 finding F-03 (Invoice/SRI without requirement) and the owner decision of 2026-11-04 to require an idempotency key; formal/system/audit-2026-10-31-phase1.md section 40.
requirements.property: For each (session, idempotencyKey) at most one invoice is created and at most one SRI script run starts: the reservation row is inserted with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING before any invoice or SRI work. Replay returns the stored response when the SHA-256 fingerprint of (session, decoded request without key and certificate password) matches; a mismatch is 409; a reservation without a response is 409. A reservation is released only when creating or linking the invoice failed, before the SRI script started. Without SRI the key is optional. Before reserving, the SRI customer is loaded and the whole SRI script request validated, so a correctable input error is a 400 that leaves the key reusable. The web client drops the key only when SRI was not requested or reported the document as issued; after an SRI error or an unconfirmed status it keeps the key, so resubmitting replays, and a new attempt needs an explicit action after checking the portal. Unresolved attempts are also kept in browser storage by fingerprint (without the certificate password), so a reload or navigation followed by the same request reuses the key; they are removed when the outcome settles or staff start a new attempt. When a request fails while an SRI attempt is unresolved (including 409 for an unanswered reservation), the error offers the same verified new-attempt action. Independently of the browser, the server refuses with 409 a new key for a session whose same request fingerprint already has an unsettled attempt (unanswered, or answered with an SRI error or a status other than issued), unless the request carries sriPortalVerified=true, which the web client sends only after the explicit verified new-attempt action.

requirements.statement: POST /login/apple verifies an Apple identity token (RS256 signature against Apple published keys, issuer, configured audiences, lifetime with 60 second skew, and nonce digest) before any database effect, then applies the same binding, linking and explicit-consent account creation rules as Google through auth_provider_identity.

account creation without explicit createNewAccount and current terms
account linking by email alone

requirements.concurrency: Per issuer:subject advisory lock shared with Google; JWKS misses and stale known keys single-flight through a cancellation-safe lock. A usable successful key set is cached for strictly less than 900 seconds; a matching kid does not extend that lifetime. Each attempted fetch reserves a 60 second cooldown before I/O, including failed, empty, or canceled attempts. Mobile rollout availability is a public build-time switch; only literal true admits native loading, cached binding reuse, button display and provider entry.
requirements.idempotency: Repeated login for a bound subject reuses the credential.
requirements.failure: Invalid or expired token yields 401 with a generic message; unconfigured audiences yield 500; key fetch failure fails closed. requirements.recovery: After key retrieval failure, unusable responses or cancellation, stale known keys fail closed during the attempt cooldown; retry retrieval after the cooldown. Failed attempts never renew successful-cache lifetime. Fresh known keys remain usable while every token signature and claim is rechecked. A backward clock cannot make a future cache timestamp fresh. Users can use email and password or link an existing account. Once the issuer migration is recorded, production schema verification requires the live NOT NULL issuer column and exact validated Google/Apple constraint; an intentional legacy prefix without that migration makes no Apple-support claim.

requirements.title: Organizer-delegated administrators of one event and courtesy tickets
requirements.statement: Only the stored organizer of an event issues, revokes and lists single-use administrator invitation links and removes delegated administrators. The first signed-in account that accepts a usable link becomes a delegated administrator of that one event; the grant is one database row, carries no global role, and stops applying when the organizer removes it. While the grant exists and the event has a stored organizer, a delegated administrator passes the organizer check for editing the event, uploading its image, creating and updating ticket tiers, listing orders and tickets, viewing ticket QR credentials, admitting tickets, planning logistics with the owner role and issuing courtesy tickets; every other organizer check, including ticket transfers, is unchanged. A courtesy issue creates one zero-amount paid order of 1 to 10 tickets for a named guest and consumes tier and event inventory through the same reservation a purchase uses, only on an active tier inside its sales window. Routes: GET /social-events/events/{eventId}/admins; GET /social-events/events/{eventId}/admin-access; POST /social-events/events/{eventId}/admin-invitations; DELETE /social-events/events/{eventId}/admin-invitations/{invitationId}; DELETE /social-events/events/{eventId}/admins/{partyId}; POST /social-events/admin-invitations/preview; POST /social-events/admin-invitations/accept; POST /social-events/events/{eventId}/courtesy-tickets.

Follows the remaining work named in formal/system/event-planning-ux.md.
requirements.property: An invitation link grants administration of exactly one event to at most one account, only while its issuer is still the stored organizer and the link is neither revoked nor expired; the raw token is never stored. A delegated administrator cannot issue, revoke or list invitations or remove administrators, and loses access when the grant row is deleted. Courtesy issuance never exceeds the inventory the shared reservation allows and never creates a nonzero amount.

requirements.authorization: Administrator management (issue, revoke, remove, invitation list) requires the stored organizer through requireEventManager and is rechecked under the event lock; strict administrators receive nothing here. The roster is readable by the organizer and by delegated administrators, who receive no invitations. Accept requires only a session and a usable token. Delegated authority is decided by delegatedEventAdminExists for the caller and event, through eventManagerPartyFor in the handlers and inside admitTicket; it applies only when the event has a stored organizer.
requirements.privacy: Only the SHA-256 digest of the token is stored; the token is returned once to the organizer and travels to the server in request bodies only. The web client carries it in the URL fragment of the public event page, removes it after use, keeps it out of login return targets and analytics URLs, and holds it across sign-in only in tab-scoped session storage keyed by event. Every unusable link receives the same 404. The link is a bearer capability until first use and the invitee name is not matched to the accepting account. Delegated administrators read order, ticket and buyer data of the event as the organizer does.
requirements.concurrency: Issue, revoke, remove, preview, accept and courtesy issuance lock the social_event row FOR UPDATE and re-read organizer, invitation and grant under it, so simultaneous acceptances admit exactly one account and acceptance, revocation, removal and courtesy issuance are ordered. Ticket admission reads the grant under the same event lock. Event edit and ticket-tier writes read the grant before their transaction, so a removal committed in between does not stop the one request already in flight.
requirements.idempotency: The accepting account may accept the same link again without change while its grant exists. Revoking a revoked invitation succeeds without change. Issuing is not idempotent: each call creates a new link. Courtesy issuance has no idempotency key: a repeated request issues another order.
requirements.failure: 400 invalid invitee name, identifier, courtesy quantity, holder name or email; 403 caller is not the organizer or an admitted delegated administrator, or the event has no organizer; 404 event missing or hidden, invitation or administrator not on this event, unusable link, tier not on this event; 409 pending-invitation limit, revoking an accepted invitation, organizer accepting their own link, a courtesy issue on an inactive tier or outside its sales window, or not enough tickets for a courtesy issue. A refused request writes nothing.
requirements.recovery: The organizer issues a new link after an expired, revoked or misdirected one, and removes an administrator who should not have accepted. No automatic retry; the web client keeps the token and offers a retry after a transient failure. The rollback script refuses to drop the tables while grants or invitations exist.
requirements.observability: HTTP status; event_admin_invitation and event_admin_member rows (creator, grantor, timestamps); courtesy order metadata naming the issuing party. No metric, log line or audit entry is added.
requirements.verification: Six PostgreSQL Hspec examples in tdf-hq/test/TDF/EventAdminDelegationSpec.hs, run through scripts/test-event-admin-delegation.sh against a fully migrated disposable database: organizer-only issue with digest-only storage; acceptance and its idempotence; binding to one account, one event and the issuer's authority; eight accounts racing for one link; revocation and removal; logistics owner role, courtesy issuance, quantity and capacity refusals and admission by a delegated administrator, refused again after removal. Jest tests cover the client calls, the organizer and delegated views, the courtesy form, the invitation panel and the removal of the token from login and analytics URLs. The hosted workflow runs the script after the organizer runner; without the runner's database variable the Hspec group reports one pending example.
requirements.evidence: formal/system/event-admin-delegation.md; local PostgreSQL 16 run of scripts/test-event-admin-delegation.sh on 2026-11-11 (6 examples, 0 failures). The runner is a step of .github/workflows/ci.yml; no hosted run of it has been observed yet.
requirements.confidence: The new handlers, the admission change and every call site of eventManagerPartyFor were read in full (transfer handlers no longer use it) and the grant lifecycle is exercised on PostgreSQL; the existing operations a delegated administrator now passes are established by reading, not by per-route tests, and there is no model.
ambiguity: The list of operations delegated, the 14-day expiry and the limits of 10 pending links and 10 tickets per courtesy order are implementation choices; owner confirmation is pending.
A delegated administrator can also create a direct zero-price ticket order for another buyer, as the organizer can.

Courtesy issuance requires an active tier inside its sales window and has no idempotency key; whether courtesy tickets should have their own quota or be reported separately in finance is undecided, and the sales-window refusal has no dedicated test.
Event edit and ticket-tier writes decide delegation before taking their transaction; one request in flight can complete after the grant is removed.
The link is a bearer capability until accepted; nobody is notified when it is accepted and the invitee name is not verified.
The routes are absent from the OpenAPI document and no Mobile client surface exists.

conformance.reason: The grant lifecycle, the single-acceptance race, removal and courtesy issuance are exercised on PostgreSQL (locally; the runner is now a hosted workflow step) and the web flows by Jest; the widened organizer checks on existing routes are covered by reading only, no model exists and the product limits await owner confirmation.
